description: Toxic mold can create serious health issues, and it hits children the hardest. What to do when a child gets sick and who may be responsible.
shortAnswer: Toxic mold can create serious health issues. It hits children the hardest. When a child becomes sick and the suspected cause is toxic mold, take pictures of the mold, get mold tests, and find a consultant to test the building. If legal action might be necessary, lining up expert testimony is essential.

faq.q: What health problems can toxic mold cause in children?
faq.a: Children who are exposed to toxic mold for a prolonged time can develop reactive airway disease, including the development of asthma, allergies and respiratory disease, wheezing, coughing and difficulty breathing. One type of toxic mold, Black Mold, may be linked to a serious lung condition in infants, called Idiopathic Pulmonary Hemorrhage, or IPH.

faq.q: Who can be sued in a toxic mold injury case?
faq.a: Prospective defendants in these lawsuits are insurance companies, architects, engineers, builders, remediation companies, landlords, manufacturers, repair services, and home sellers.

faq.q: Does insurance cover a child's injuries from toxic mold if the policy has a mold exclusion?
faq.a: Since 2003 virtually all property and liability policies have come to contain mold or fungus exclusions. But water leaks are a primary cause of mold growth and are generally covered by insurance. If the mold that harmed your child was caused by a water leak that is a covered loss, the insurance company may be responsible.

faq.q: Is a toxic mold claim worth bringing?
faq.a: Toxic mold cases are expensive to bring and win. For that reason there must be significant damages (high medical bills or permanent impairment) before you and an attorney can justify the costs of bringing a claim.
